record.Etymology: 176. Brah. rōta ‘root’ and rōtk ‘root; fibre, strand, string; woof’ seems to be Iranian borrowing because of Bal. rōtag resp. rótag ‘root’ which, however, can hardly be a reflex of PIE *wréh2ds ‘root’.

proposal.evidence: Bray (1934), s.v. rota, explicitly identifies Balochi rotag; his subsequent question concerns its deeper connection to grow words, not the Balochi form itself. Zoller (2023), p.851 independently proposes Iranian borrowing and supplies Balochi rótag root. The existing Balochi attestation is the immediate proposed donor; preserve Brahui final -a versus donor -ag. Bray was checked in the digitized OCR text, not a visually verified scan.
